capabilities: navigate table cells with column-aware arrow keys and working Page Up/Down
skip Markdown syntax with smart Home
split Chinese and Japanese words for keyboard movement, deletion, and double-click selection
fix Vim motions (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, gg/G) inside tables and add leader-key table row/column commands
provide Emacs-style cursor movement, kill and yank, and case conversion commands
disambiguation: Not just a hotkey remapper; its commands add table-aware and CJK-aware cursor behavior on top of keys you already use.
extras: Development was AI-assisted per the README's acknowledgments; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Full documentation lives on an external site in English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese.
intentEvidence: This makes Obsidian's built-in Vim mode handle Markdown tables naturally.
motivation: The author thinks Live Preview renders and edits tables well but falls short in this one specific way, and built the plugin to close that gap and raise the baseline for cursor movement in Obsidian.
problem: Obsidian's cursor keys, Page Up/Down, Home, and built-in Vim mode misbehave inside Live Preview Markdown tables, and word movement treats Chinese/Japanese text as unbroken runs.
summary: Cursor-movement plugin that makes arrow keys, Home/End, and word motions table-aware in Live Preview, with Chinese/Japanese word splitting for default keys, Vim mode, and Emacs keybindings.
